rows.title: Attempt on Convergence of the holomorphic observable of the honeycomb self-avoiding walk to a conformal covariant
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Same structure as C0050: contour relations plus Morera give holomorphy of subsequential limits; identify the missing a priori bounds. Result: Smirnov's parafermionic observable for the honeycomb SAW at the critical weight satisfies the discrete contour relation (sum around each hexagon vanishes) but is not discretely holomorphic (only half the Cauchy-Riemann relations), the same deficit as for FK with q not 2. Any subsequential limit of the normalised observable that is tight and locally bounded is holomorphic by Morera (the contour relations pass to the limit) with boundary modulus determined by the spin 5/8 and the boundary conditions; the function (Phi')^{5/8} is the unique such function with the prescribed singularity at a and normalisation at b. Hence Conjecture 3.6 reduces to (i) tightness/local boundedness of F_delta(a, z)/F_delta(a, b) away from a and b and (ii) control near the marked points. (i) would follow from the Beurling-type estimate that a SAW from a to z in the domain has weight comparable to the two-point function in the bulk, i.e. from an RSW-type theory for the critical SAW, which is unavailable (there is no RSW for SAW, unlike FK with q in [1,4]). So the obstruction is specific: SAW lacks the crossing estimates that make the FK reduction work. Obstruction: No RSW-type crossing estimates for critical SAW; tightness of the observable ratio is not available.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0095-convergence-of-the-holomorphic-observable-of-the-honeycomb-self-avoidi
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Attempt on Convergence of the parafermionic observable to (phi')^sigma for q <= 4
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Test the conjecture's consistency by the boundary values and the contour relations alone. Result: The contour relations plus the known boundary values determine the discrete observable up to a subspace of dimension equal to the number of faces minus the number of independent contour relations, which is of the order of the number of vertices, so the observable is far from determined by what is proved; the conjecture is a statement about the actual random-cluster measure, not derivable from the relations alone. A weaker rigorous consequence that IS available: the contour relations imply that the integral of f_delta along any closed contour vanishes, so any subsequential limit of (2 delta)^{-sigma} f_delta, if tight, is holomorphic (Morera), and its boundary behaviour (modulus fixed on the boundary arcs by the boundary conditions) makes (phi')^sigma the unique candidate if the limit is bounded near a and b. Hence the conjecture reduces to tightness plus a priori bounds near the marked points. This reduction is standard for q = 2 and I confirmed it goes through for all q <= 4 given the contour relations; the a priori bounds are the missing input. Key identity: Contour relations + Morera => any tight subsequential limit is holomorphic with the prescribed boundary modulus; uniqueness then forces (phi')^sigma. Obstruction: Tightness and boundary a priori bounds for the observable are unproved for q not 2.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0050-convergence-of-the-parafermionic-observable-to-phi-sigma-for-q-4
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Attempt on Hexagonal self-avoiding-walk scaling limit
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Exact finite-domain conditional law Result: For a finite-graph a-to-b self-avoiding path with weight z^length, condition on an initial simple prefix. The remaining path has the same fugacity law on the graph with earlier prefix vertices removed. The factor z^prefix_length cancels between numerator and partition function. Check: The endpoint stays in the graph; deleting it would invalidate the argument. Fixed-length conditioning also fixes the remaining length and is a different ensemble. Obstruction: This domain Markov property supplies neither tightness nor conformal invariance and does not identify an SLE scaling limit.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-p0003-hexagonal-self-avoiding-walk-scaling-limit
No independent review

rows.title: Attempt on Interfaces of the honeycomb O(n) loop model converge to SLE(kappa)
rows.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD, author-checked only, from the 2026-09-07 intake. Method: Check which n have any discrete holomorphic observable and which have crossing estimates. Result: Duminil-Copin-Smirnov's parafermionic observable exists for all n in [0,2] at the critical x with spin sigma = 1 - 3 arccos(-n/2)/(4 pi)... (the spin depends on n) and satisfies the contour relations; full holomorphicity holds for none except the Ising-related n = 1 dilute? (n = 1 corresponds to the Ising model's low-temperature expansion on the honeycomb, for which the observable is the Ising fermion and IS holomorphic — that is how Smirnov's Ising result and Chelkak-Smirnov work; on the honeycomb the n = 1 loop model at x_c is the critical Ising model, so the n = 1 case at the critical point IS known via Ising, contrary to the naive reading; the source's remark 'n = 1 site percolation' refers to the dense phase x = 1, kappa = 6). So: n = 1 critical (Ising, SLE(3)) and n = 1 dense (percolation, SLE(6)) are both known; n = 2 corresponds to kappa = 4 (GFF level lines) and is open; n in (0,1) union (1,2) open in both phases; n = 0 critical open (P0003), n = 0 dense (kappa = 8, uniform spanning tree-like, x = 1: the dense O(0) model at x = 1 is the Hamiltonian-cycle-type model... open). RSW-type crossing estimates for the O(n) model are known for n in [1,2] (Duminil-Copin-Glazman-Peled-Spinka, 2020) giving tightness of interfaces; identification of the limit needs the holomorphicity, which only n = 1 has. Rigorous partial: the conjecture at n = 1 is a theorem in both phases; for n in (1,2] tightness holds and only identification is missing; for n in [0,1) even tightness (crossing estimates) is missing. Key identity: n = 1 critical honeycomb O(n) = critical Ising (holomorphic fermion, SLE(3) proved); n = 1 dense = site percolation (SLE(6) proved). Obstruction: Holomorphicity fails for n not 1; crossing estimates unavailable for n < 1.
Refers to the open problem node open-problem-c0096-interfaces-of-the-honeycomb-o-n-loop-model-converge-to-sle-kappa
No independent review; result status attempted_unsolved

rows.title: Open problem: Convergence of the holomorphic observable of the honeycomb self-avoiding walk to a conformal covariant
rows.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For the critical honeycomb self-avoiding walk in a simply connected domain with marked boundary points a, b, the ratio F_delta(a_delta, z_delta)/F_delta(a_delta, b_delta) of the discrete holomorphic observable converges as delta -> 0 to (Phi'(z)/Phi'(b))^{5/8}, with Phi the conformal map to the upper half-plane sending a to infinity. Source: Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012, Conjecture 3.6, p. 23.
Posed in Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07

rows.title: Open problem: Convergence of the parafermionic observable to (phi')^sigma for q <= 4
rows.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For the critical random-cluster model with q <= 4, the vertex parafermionic observable f_delta satisfies (2 delta)^{-sigma} f_delta -> (phi')^sigma where phi maps the domain to the strip R x (0,1) with a, b sent to -infinity, +infinity. Source: Duminil-Copin: Lectures on the Ising and Potts models on the hypercubic lattice, PIMS 2017, Conjecture 4 (Smirnov), p. 94.

rows.title: Open problem: Interfaces of the honeycomb O(n) loop model converge to SLE(kappa)
rows.body:
OPEN PROBLEM (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status attempted_unsolved). For n in [0, 2] and x = 1/sqrt(2 + sqrt(2 - n)) the honeycomb O(n) loop-model interface converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/(2 pi - arccos(-n/2)); for x above that value it converges to SLE(kappa) with kappa = 4 pi/arccos(-n/2). Known only for n = 1 at the critical point (site percolation, Smirnov) and for the n = 0 boundary in the trivial sense. Source: Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012, Conjecture 3.7, p. 25. Status notes: The n = 0 critical case is the SLE(8/3) conjecture for SAW (the source's Conjecture 1.5), which the Codex campaign already records as P0003 (hexagonal SAW scaling limit); this record covers n in (0,2] and the dense phase, and the n = 0 dense case (x above critical, kappa = 8).
Posed in Bauerschmidt, Duminil-Copin, Goodman, Slade: Lectures on self-avoiding walks, Clay 2012
Current status unverified as of 2026-09-07
